One in Christ
WUHN in KRYST
noun phrase (doctrine of the church)
From the Pauline phrase heis en Christo (Gal 3:28), one in Christ; the gospel unity of all believers in the one body of the Lord.

Biblical Definition

To be one in Christ is to share, with all the redeemed, a common standing and a common life in the Lord Jesus, by whom the ancient division between Jew and Gentile is abolished. Paul declares, "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus" (Gal 3:28). Christ "is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us" (Eph 2:14), reconciling Jew and Gentile in one body unto God by the cross (Eph 2:16). This unity is real, deep, and gracious: every believer, whatever his nation or station, is justified by the same faith, indwelt by the same Spirit, and an heir of the same promise. Yet this oneness in Christ does NOT erase the creational order God established before the fall. Galatians speaks of equal standing in justification, not the abolition of sex or office; the same apostle who wrote "neither male nor female" also ordered male-only eldership and creational headship in the home and the church. The progressive reading that presses Gal 3:28 to dissolve the two sexes, to ordain women, or to bless same-sex unions twists a text about gospel access into a charter for autonomy. This dictionary confesses that all believers are gloriously one in Christ, while the distinctions of sex and office that God wove into creation abide.

Webster 1828 Definition

To be one in Christ is to share a common standing and life in the Lord, Jew and Gentile reconciled in one body. The middle wall of partition is broken down by the cross. This unity does not erase the creational order of sex and office.

ONE IN CHRIST, noun phrase. The gospel unity of all believers, joined in one body by their common standing in the Lord Jesus.

It abolishes the old division between Jew and Gentile and levels every distinction of nation or station before the cross.

"There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus" (Gal 3:28).

It requires brotherly love and equal honor among the saints; it forbids the partitions of pride that the world raises.

It concerns equal standing in justification, not the dissolving of the creational order of sex and office.

Key Scripture

Gal 3:28 — "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus."

Eph 2:14 — "For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us."

Eph 2:16 — "And that he might reconcile both unto God in one body by the cross, having slain the enmity thereby."

Col 3:11 — "Where there is neither Greek nor Jew, circumcision nor uncircumcision, Barbarian, Scythian, bond nor free: but Christ is all, and in all."

Modern Corruption

The progressive movement seizes Galatians 3:28 to abolish the creational distinctions of sex and office, turning a text about gospel access into a charter for women's ordination, gender ideology, and affirming sexuality.

expand to see more

Affirming and egalitarian teachers read "neither male nor female" as though Paul had erased the two sexes God made in creation, and so they ordain women to the eldership, baptize transgender self-definition, and bless same-sex unions in the name of inclusion. But the apostle is plainly speaking of equal access to justifying grace, for Jew and Gentile, slave and free, man and woman alike are heirs of Abraham by faith. The very letters that proclaim this oneness also command wives to submit, restrict the eldership to qualified men, and root these orders in creation, not culture. To pit Galatians 3 against 1 Timothy 2 is to set the Spirit against Himself.

Recover the true and glorious unity: one Lord, one faith, one baptism, one body in which the wall between the nations is forever down. This unity does not flatten the good order God wove into our creation as male and female, nor the offices He appointed in His church. Equal standing before God and distinct callings within His order are both gifts of the same wise Lord, and the church flourishes when she holds them together.

Hebrew Roots

The phrase grows from Paul's heis en Christo and the image of the broken middle wall of partition.

expand to see more

Greek heis, one, in Gal 3:28 stresses a single shared standing, not a single undifferentiated mass.

The phrase en Christo, in Christ, names the union by which believers share His life and benefits.

Greek mesotoichon, the "middle wall" of Eph 2:14, pictures the temple barrier between Jew and Gentile.

The context of Gal 3 is sonship and inheritance by faith, defining the kind of oneness in view.

Col 3:11 parallels the list, climaxing in "Christ is all, and in all," the center of the union.

Usage

"Being one in Christ, the freed slave and his former master sat at the same Table as brothers."

"He cherished the oneness believers have in Christ without ever pretending it dissolved the offices of the church."

"The teacher abused "neither male nor female" to ordain women, mistaking gospel access for the erasure of order."
